name: Times club monthly special crossword No 272

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old governors of Channel island in retreat, with lots of poetry

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the island's name is read backwards

blocks.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island in the English Channel
W is a standard abbreviation for with
odes are poems, so several of them make a lot of poetry

explanation.surface: Some historical rulers of a Channel island retire there and fill their days writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: WOI + W + ODES. Woiwodes (or voivodes) were governors of provinces in Poland and the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: A woiwode was a provincial ruler in eastern Europe, an archaic title, hence governors of old.

clue.text: Looking up a mild oath, formerly something unacceptable in native language

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading from the bottom upwards, so everything before the definition is reversed

blocks.note: taken as written
Gad! is an old-fashioned euphemism for God used as a mild exclamation
a no-no is something not allowed

explanation.surface: Someone glances up, mutters an outdated oath and lets slip something unacceptable in their mother tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAD NONO, read upwards, gives ONONDAGA. 'Native' here means Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: Onondaga is the Iroquoian tongue spoken by the Onondaga people of New York State, a Native American language.

clue.text: Clock northern comedian and Times hack, unlikely hosts

definitions.note: a clock in northern English and Scottish dialect

indicators.note: a host takes in guests, so the word for unlikely has the word for hack placed inside it

blocks.note: a wag is a joker or wit
times as in multiplication, as in five by three
a tall story is an unlikely one
to hack is to chop or hew

explanation.surface: A northern comic and a Times journalist are clocked, though they seem improbable as hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG + BY + T(HEW)ALL. 'Clock' looks like a verb meaning to spot; it is the noun the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag-by-the-wall is a dialect name in northern England and Scotland for a hanging wall clock with exposed pendulum.

clue.text: Irish food: one way to reverse what the Polish brought up?

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the letters for one way are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
polishing brings up a shine on a surface

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about Irish cooking and whether Polish people turn things round when serving.
explanation.walkthrough: I RD backwards gives DRI, then SHEEN. The capital P disguises polish, the shine, as the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Drisheen is a traditional Cork blood pudding, a dish particular to Ireland.

clue.text: Small place of worship using English for Mass: one’s above all that?

indicators.note: using one thing for another means swapping it in, so the letter for English replaces the letter for mass

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a temple is a building for worship
E is the abbreviation for English
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A tiny chapel holds its Mass in English rather than Latin, rising above the old rites.
explanation.walkthrough: S + TEMPLE with its M swapped for E gives STEEPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tower with a spire rising high over a church, so it stands above the whole building.

clue.text: Couple retaining place for US singer

indicators.note: retaining something means keeping it held inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: to couple things is to join them
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A pair hang on to a booking or venue reserved for an American performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Janis Joplin was an American rock and blues vocalist of the late 1960s.

clue.text: Island sinking in foul marsh on the veldt?

indicators.note: something sinking drops from its place, so the letter leaves its spot and reappears at the bottom of the down entry

blocks.note: foul means vile
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island gradually going under in a stinking South African swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: In VILE the I moves down to the end, giving VLEI. The veldt is South African grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlei is an Afrikaans word for low-lying ground that floods in the wet season, a South African swamp.

clue.text: Sit with lungs heaving, making convulsive gasps no more

indicators.note: heaving suggests violent churning motion, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sits with chest heaving, giving out spasmodic gulps of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Singults are sobs or hiccups, an obsolete word, hence spasmodic breaths that are no longer in use.

clue.text: Old temple: that’s found empty, and pub, the first now the last one

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outermost letters standing
the opening letter of the word for pub is moved round to the end

blocks.note: that's refers back to the word temple, whose outside letters are kept
a local is the pub nearest one's home
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient shrine turns out bare and has become a pub, with the old order reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' points back to temple, emptied to TE; LOCAL becomes OCALL; then I. A local is British for one's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A teocalli was an Aztec pyramid topped by a shrine, an ancient Mexican place of worship.

clue.text: Problem describing heterosexual relationship when there’s no one right or left

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letters for one, right and left are taken away

blocks.note: a boy-girl relationship is one between the sexes
the Roman numeral for one
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An agony-column note on the trouble in a straight couple's relationship when no one is right or left.
explanation.walkthrough: BOYGIRL loses I, R and L to leave BOYG. The Boyg is the shapeless obstacle Peer Gynt meets in Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: From Ibsen, a boyg is any formless, intractable obstacle that is hard to get to grips with, so a difficulty.

clue.text: Writing as biographer, I go after something startling said to be expansive

indicators.note: after places the pieces for I and go behind the preceding material in the answer

blocks.note: bo or boo is the exclamation said to startle someone
to swell is to grow larger and expand
taken as written
go in the sense of energy or vim, also called zing

explanation.surface: A writer turns to biography, chasing some sensational story that is supposedly expansive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun for energy, not the verb, and 'after' sends I and it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the famous life of Samuel Johnson, so to boswellize is to compose a detailed biography in his manner.

clue.text: Doctors veg, mostly reversing contradictory advice for insectivore

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for veg is dropped
reversing means going backwards, so the doctors and veg pieces are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body
to veg out is to laze about
do and don't are opposite instructions

explanation.surface: Medics loafing about while dispensing mixed messages about an insect-eating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers only the doctors and veg pieces; the contradictory advice follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Zalambdodont mammals such as tenrecs and golden moles have V-ridged molars and feed on insects and grubs.

clue.text: Dusky swimmer no longer comes out with energy

blocks.note: saith is the archaic form of says, as in comes out with a remark
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned swimmer has retired and now emerges full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes out with' is read as says, given in its old form.
explanation.definitionFit: The saithe or coley is a dark-backed North Atlantic fish of the cod family, also called the coalfish.

clue.text: Perfume ingredient maybe occupying some ladies in the fifties

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the pair of fifties

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties
occupying a place means being in it
a in the sense of one or some
the ladies is a British name for a women's toilet, and a loo is a toilet

explanation.surface: Perhaps a scent used by women of a certain age, lingering in the washroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fifties' supplies two Ls, which sit either side of the rest. 'Maybe' marks the definition as one example of an ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Linalool is a fragrant alcohol from lavender and coriander used widely in scents, an example of a perfumery component.

clue.text: A very filling meal that’s later grabbed near revolving restaurant

indicators.note: filling puts something inside, so the A and very abbreviation go into the meal
grabbed means seized and held, so the result holds the next piece
revolving means turning round, so the abbreviation for near is read backwards

blocks.note: tea is a meal taken later in the day
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
NR is the abbreviation for near

explanation.surface: A hearty supper eaten late is snapped up near a rotating eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions happen in turn: first the A and V go into the meal, then that result grabs the turned abbreviation before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating house serving food and wine, a kind of informal dining place.

clue.text: Choke by informally and very quietly pressing on outside of ligature

indicators.note: pressing on means pushing up against, so the pieces sit side by side
the outside of a word is its two end letters only

blocks.note: thro' is the informal spelling of through, meaning by
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A strangling described with casual, hushed pressure on a binding cord.
explanation.walkthrough: THRO + PP + LE. 'By' as through, as in going by the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Thropple is a dialect word for the throat or windpipe, and as a verb it means to throttle or strangle.

clue.text: A lot of clever people for one genetically modified idiot

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
GM is the usual abbreviation for genetically modified
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Plenty of bright sparks, and yet one of them is a GM-engineered fool.
explanation.walkthrough: EG + GM + ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggmass is slang for intellectuals collectively, from egghead, so a body of brainy types.

clue.text: Leg raised in the morning, a hand likewise, making decorative figures

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned to read upwards, so the morning abbreviation is reversed
likewise says the next piece is treated the same way, so it is read upwards too

blocks.note: gam is slang for a leg
a.m. means in the morning
to give a hand is to aid

explanation.surface: An exercise routine: a leg lifted at dawn and an arm likewise, posing in ornamental shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM + AM upwards + AID upwards. 'Leg raised' looks like one unit, but raised applies to the morning piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammadia are ornaments made of the Greek capital gamma, found on church vestments and in mosaics.

clue.text: Sons switch positions, the second occupying two steam-holes

indicators.note: occupying means living inside, so the second switch position goes inside the two

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a switch has two positions, the first of which is used here
the Roman numeral for two
the second of the two switch positions

explanation.surface: Male offspring trade places, with the younger one moving in among two vents of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: S + OFF + I(ON)I. Switch positions are off and on, so they supply two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soffioni are volcanic vents emitting jets of vapour, notably in Tuscany, so openings that blow out steam.

clue.text: Flounce out of a party, upset after brief stumble

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue these letters are turned to read upwards
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for stumble goes

blocks.note: a stumble is a fall
taken as written
Lab is short for the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: A politician storms out of the party, angry after a minor trip.
explanation.walkthrough: FAL(L) + A LAB turned up. 'Flounce' looks like a verb meaning storm off; it is the noun for a frill.
explanation.definitionFit: A falbala is a trimming or frill on a dress or petticoat, the same kind of ornament as a furbelow.

clue.text: Furniture maker’s shareware warranted being scaled down

indicators.note: scaled down means reduced in size, so only a part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words after the first three

explanation.surface: A cabinet-maker's free software is guaranteed, though in a cut-down form.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a tree, which makes furniture by supplying the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The rewarewa is a New Zealand tree whose mottled timber is prized for cabinetwork, so it supplies material for chairs and tables.

clue.text: Daughter’s right to withhold the odd stuff from personnel, coy

indicators.note: withholding the odd ones means keeping back the first, third, fifth and so on, so only the even ones count

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and every other letter

explanation.surface: A shy daughter claims her entitlement to keep strange items back from the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Esnecy is the old legal privilege of the eldest coheiress to choose her share first when an inheritance is divided.

clue.text: Put a dampener on old woman with challenge

blocks.note: the old woman is slang for one's mother, ma
to defy is to challenge

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the mood of their mother by squaring up to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a dampener on' reads as discourage; it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Madefy is a rare verb meaning to moisten or make wet, so literally to make damp.

clue.text: Unruly band pillaging area’s left swine out of work!

indicators.note: left in the sense of departed, so the area abbreviation goes from the fodder
unruly means disorderly, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A rowdy gang loot the district and the pigs are left jobless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' looks like unemployed; it means taken from a literary work, a Beatrix Potter book.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigling Bland is the pig hero of Beatrix Potter's Tale of Pigling Bland, so a hog from a published book.

clue.text: Holes, one graphically represented, in flooded forest

blocks.note: a gap is a hole or opening
a hole drawn as a shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Puddles, one drawn on a map, appear in a waterlogged wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holes' covers both pieces: GAP, and an O as a drawn hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Gapo is Amazonian riverside woodland that is seasonally submerged when the rivers rise.

clue.text: Coin once passed on, behold sent back

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word for behold is read backwards

blocks.note: ob., short for Latin obiit, means died, as on gravestones
lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: An old piece of money handed down, and look, it was returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' looks like handed over; it means died. The ancient Greeks put this coin in the mouth of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver piece of ancient Greek currency, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: To the west, large area of land Yank mostly used for festival

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means right to left, so the whole piece is read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for yank is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
an acre is a measured area of land
to yank is to pull sharply

explanation.surface: An American heads west and puts a big plot of land to use for a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lupercal, or Lupercalia, was an ancient Roman fertility celebration held each February.

clue.text: Form of disease found in spruce, regrettably, earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the word for regrettably comes before the word for spruce

blocks.note: alas is said regretfully
spruce means neat and trim

explanation.surface: Sadly, a blight has been detected in a spruce tree before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the conifer; it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastrim is a mild variety of smallpox, also called variola minor.
